clues: This city is in the north of Sweden. It sits by a river, a short way from the Bothnian Bay.
Winters here are long and cold, with deep snow, yet the bay softens the cold a bit. That help from the sea gives warm summers for a place this far north.
This place was made a city in 1845. It then grew fast, and it reached its full size by the 1960s.
This town is well known for ice hockey, and its top team has won the top league more than once. The whole town is known for the game.
Gold mining was a huge part of work here in the past. That is why folks gave the place a Swedish nickname that means gold town.
